Rashi on Chullin 74a:10:1.hebrew: ולהאי תנא - דברייתא, דפריך מינא דאמיה, וסבר "יש במינו שחיטה" קרינא ביה:
Rashi on Chullin 74a:10:1.english: And according to that tanna - of the baraita, who raises a refutation [based on] its mother's kind, and holds that we apply to it [the principle that] "there is slaughter in its kind":

Rashi on Chullin 74a:10:2.hebrew: טרפה דשחיטה מטהרתה מנא ליה - תיפוק ליה מבהמה טמאה, דאין שחיטה מטהרתה:
Rashi on Chullin 74a:10:2.english: [A] tereifa, that slaughter purifies it — from where does he [derive it] - Let him derive it from an impure animal, whose slaughter does not purify it:

Rashi on Chullin 74a:11:1.hebrew: ושחט בה בן ט' חי - ויצא אחר שחיטתו ואמו קיימת. בן ח' לא קא מיבעי ליה, דהא אפילו יצא לאויר העולם ושחטו, תנן במתניתין (לעיל חולין דף עב:) "אין שחיטתו מטהרתו":
Rashi on Chullin 74a:11:1.english: And slaughtered a live nine-[month-old fetus] inside it - and [the fetus] came out after its slaughter while its mother was [still] alive. He does not raise a dilemma regarding an eight-[month-old fetus], for even if it came out into the open air of the world and one slaughtered it, we learned in the Mishnah (above, Chullin 72b) [that] its slaughter does not render it permitted:

Rashi on Chullin 74a:12:1.hebrew: אבל במעי אמו לא שריא - שחיטה דיליה, וכ"ש לרבנן דאמרי לא שייכא ביה שחיטה כלל, אפילו יצא חי לאחר שחיטה, דאין שחיטה בו אלא ביצא לאויר בחיי אמו:
Rashi on Chullin 74a:12:1.english: But inside its mother, [it] does not render permitted - [meaning] its own slaughter [does not render the fetus permitted]; and all the more so according to the Rabbis, who say that slaughter does not apply to it at all, even if it emerged alive after [its mother's] slaughter, for slaughter applies to it only when it emerged into the open air during its mother's lifetime:

Rashi on Chullin 74a:13:1.hebrew: או דילמא אפי' לרבנן - שריא ליה שחיטתו, דקסברי רבנן ד' סימנין אכשר ביה רחמנא, באיזה שני הסימנים שישחטו — או של אמו או שלו; וכ"ש לרבי מאיר דאמר שחיטה שייכא ביה:
Rashi on Chullin 74a:13:1.english: Or perhaps even according to the Rabbis - its [own] slaughter permits it, for the Rabbis hold [that] the Merciful One rendered four simanim fit [for slaughtering it], [meaning] whichever two simanim are slaughtered — whether [those] of its mother or [those] of its own; and all the more so according to Rabbi Meir, who says [that] slaughter is applicable to it:

Rashi on Chullin 74a:14:1.hebrew: ת"ש - דתנן במתני': "הרי שנולדה טרפה מן הבטן מנין", וקס"ד דאפילו בנטרפה שעה אחת קודם לידתה קאמר, דלא היתה לה שעת הכושר לישחט, ולא חל עליה תורת שחיטה:
Rashi on Chullin 74a:14:1.english: Come [and] hear - For we learned in the Mishnah: "[If] it was born a tereifa from the womb, from where [do we know that it is forbidden]?" And we initially assumed that [the Mishnah] is speaking even of [a case] where it became a tereifa one hour before its birth, [implying] that it never had a period of potential fitness to be slaughtered, and the law of ritual slaughter never took effect upon it:

Rashi on Chullin 74a:14:2.hebrew: ואם איתא - דשחיטה במעי אמו שחיטה היא, הרי היתה לטרפה זו שעת הכושר לשחיטה קודם שנטרפה:
Rashi on Chullin 74a:14:2.english: And if it is [so] - that slaughtering [a fetus] in its mother's womb is [a valid] slaughter, then this tereifa had a period of fitness for slaughter before it became a tereifa:

Rashi on Chullin 74a:15:1.hebrew: בבעלת ה' רגלים - דהאי טרפות ודאי הוה בה משנוצרה, וכגון שיתור זה ברגלים האחרונים, דאמר בבכורות (דף מ.) דבעלת ה' רגלים הרי זה מום, ואמרי' התם: לא שנו אלא שחסר או יתר ביד, אבל ברגל אפילו טרפה נמי הוי, דכל יתר כנטול דמי:
Rashi on Chullin 74a:15:1.english: [Where a fetus] has five legs - For this tereifa status was certainly present in it from the moment it was formed, and [this refers to a case] where this extra [limb] is among the hind legs, as it says in Bekhorot (40a) that [an animal] with five legs — this is a blemish, and we say there: they only taught [this] where [a limb] is missing or extra in the foreleg, but in the hind leg it is even a tereifa as well, for any extra [limb] is considered as if it were removed.

Rashi on Chullin 74a:16:1.hebrew: קורעו - שאין צריך שחיטה, ומודי ר"מ בהו דאיתרבו מ"כל בבהמה תאכלו", דלאו חדשים איכא ולאו אוירא איכא, הילכך לאו בהמה הוא:
Rashi on Chullin 74a:16:1.english: He tears it open - for it does not require slaughter, and Rabbi Meir agrees regarding these [fetuses] that they are included from [the verse], "anything in an animal you may eat" [Deuteronomy 14:6], for there are neither [completed] months nor [breathing of] air; therefore, it is not [considered an independent] animal:

Rashi on Chullin 74a:16:2.hebrew: ומוציא את דמו - דחלבו הוא דמותר, כדקתני לקמן (חולין דף עה.): מה חלב ושתי הכליות האמורין באשם מוצא מכלל שליל, אף כל מוצא מכלל שליל; אבל דמו לא גרע מדם האברים, דקי"ל בכריתות (דף כא:): דם האברים עובר בלא תעשה:
Rashi on Chullin 74a:16:2.english: And removes its blood - For [only] its forbidden fat is permitted, as it is taught later (Chullin 75a): Just as the fat and the two kidneys stated regarding a guilt-offering are excluded from the category of a fetus, so too all [such fat] is excluded from the category of a fetus; however, its blood is no less [stringent] than the blood of limbs, as we hold in Keritot (21b): [for] the blood of limbs, one transgresses a negative commandment:

Rashi on Chullin 74a:17:1.hebrew: טעון שחיטה - דחדשים גרמי לשוייה בהמה באנפי נפשיה, ולא איתרבאי מ"כל בבהמה תאכלו". ולרבנן, חדשים ולידה גרמי, דרבנן מרבו ליה להיתרא מ"כל בבהמה תאכלו":
Rashi on Chullin 74a:17:1.english: It requires slaughter - For [the completion of its] months [of gestation] causes it to be rendered an animal in its own right, and it is not included [in the permit derived] from "all [that is] within the animal you may eat." Whereas according to the Rabbis, [both] months [of gestation] and birth cause [it to become an independent animal], for the Rabbis include it for permissibility from "all [that is] within the animal you may eat":

Rashi on Chullin 74a:17:2.english: And one is liable for [violating the prohibition of] "itself and its offspring" - [meaning] that one may not slaughter it on the day that they slaughtered its mother:

Rashi on Chullin 74a:1:1.english: There is not in them - the negative prohibition of a limb from a living animal:

Rashi on Chullin 74a:1:2.hebrew: אלא מצות פרוש - בעלמא מדרבנן, וקרא אסמכתא בעלמא. אלמא אין שחיטה עושה ניפול:
Rashi on Chullin 74a:1:2.english: Only a mitzva to separate - merely by rabbinic decree, and the verse is merely an asmakhta [a scriptural support]. Evidently, slaughter does not render [the limb as having] fallen off:

Rashi on Chullin 74a:2:1.english: [If] one ate this - [meaning] the dangling limb:

Rashi on Chullin 74a:2:2.english: He is not flogged - because it is merely a mitzvah to abstain [from eating it]:

Rashi on Chullin 74a:3:1.english: He turned [his face] away - in anger:

Rashi on Chullin 74a:3:2.hebrew: כי אמרי אנא - דלוקה משום אבר מן החי, במיתה דעושה ניפול, ואשמיעך רב דלא משום נבלה מתרינן ביה, אלא משום אבר מן החי:
Rashi on Chullin 74a:3:2.english: When I said - [that one is] flogged on account of a limb from a living [animal, I was referring to] death, which renders [the limb as having] fallen [off], and Rav is teaching you that we do not warn him on account of nevelah [an unslaughtered carcass], but rather on account of a limb from a living [animal]:

Rashi on Chullin 74a:4:1.english: And anything that - [This verse] is written regarding creeping animals:

Rashi on Chullin 74a:4:2.english: Derived from "of their carcass" - [As it is written:] "And if [any] of their carcass falls":

Rashi on Chullin 74a:4:3.hebrew: אלא - הכי קאמר: "כל אשר יפול מהם במותם" — על ידי מיתה הויא נפילה; "מהם" — איברים המדולדלים בהם:
Rashi on Chullin 74a:4:3.english: Rather - This is what [the verse] means: "anything that falls from them when they are dead" — through death there is a falling; "from them" — [referring to] limbs that are dangling from them:

Rashi on Chullin 74a:5:1.hebrew: בשרצים כתיב - דלא שייכא בהו שחיטה, והיכי ממעטת שחיטה מהאי קרא:
Rashi on Chullin 74a:5:1.english: [The verse] is written with regard to creeping animals - to which slaughter does not apply, so how do you exclude slaughter from this verse?

Rashi on Chullin 74a:5:2.hebrew: אם אינו ענין כו' - דעל כרחך "במותם" מיעוטא הוא, דלגופיה לא איצטריך, דהא במתים משתעי, ד"נבלתם" כתיב; ונכתוב "וכי יפול" למימרא דעושים ניפול, ולא בעי "במותם", אלא על כרחך למעוטי שחיטה:
Rashi on Chullin 74a:5:2.english: If it has no application, etc. - For perforce, "when they are dead" is an exclusion, as it is not needed for its own sake, since [the verse] is speaking of dead [creatures], as "their carcass" is written. Let [Scripture] write "and when it falls" to indicate that [death] renders [a hanging limb as though it had] fallen off, and it would not need "when they are dead"; rather, perforce, [it comes] to exclude slaughter:

Rashi on Chullin 74a:5:3.hebrew: דלאו בני שחיטה נינהו - ולא איצטריך "במותם", דהא אפילו שחיטתם מיתה היא:
Rashi on Chullin 74a:5:3.english: Which are not subject to slaughter - and [the phrase] "when they are dead" is not needed [for creeping animals], for even their slaughter is [considered] death:

Rashi on Chullin 74a:6:1.hebrew: כעין מיתה - כעין שעת מיתה שהיו לחים, למעוטי שרץ שיבש:
Rashi on Chullin 74a:6:1.english: Similar to death - Similar to the time of [their] death, when they were moist — to exclude a creeping creature that has dried out:

Rashi on Chullin 74a:7:1.hebrew: דעובר חי - דיש במינו שחיטה, מהניא שחיטה אף לאבר היוצא לטהרו:
Rashi on Chullin 74a:7:1.english: [The limb] of a living fetus - since slaughter applies to its kind, [the mother's] slaughter is effective even for the limb that emerged, to render it [ritually] pure:

Rashi on Chullin 74a:8:1.hebrew: והתניא - בתורת כהנים, גבי "וכי ימות מן הבהמה" כו':
Rashi on Chullin 74a:8:1.english: And isn't it taught [in a baraita] - in Torat Kohanim, regarding [the verse] "And if [any] of the beasts dies," etc.:

Rashi on Chullin 74a:8:2.hebrew: בן ח' יוכיח שאע"פ שיש במינו שחיטה אין שחיטה מטהרתו - אם נולד ושחטו, אבל אגב אמו ניתר בשחיטת אמו דברי הכל; אף טריפה, אע"פ שיש במינה שחיטה, לא תטהרנה שחיטתה. ומתני' קתני: בן ח' אין במינו שחיטה:
Rashi on Chullin 74a:8:2.english: An eight-[month-old fetus] will prove [it], as even though there is slaughter in its kind, slaughter does not render it pure - [This applies] if it was born and one slaughtered it; however, [while] with its mother, it is permitted through its mother's slaughter according to everyone. So too a tereifa, even though there is slaughter in its kind, its slaughter will not render it pure. And [yet] our Mishnah teaches: An eight-[month-old fetus] has no slaughter in its kind:

Rashi on Chullin 74a:9:1.hebrew: אמר רב כהנא - האי דקתני תנא דברייתא "יש במינו שחיטה", אגב אמו קאמר, שניתר בשחיטת אמו:
Rashi on Chullin 74a:9:1.english: Rav Kahana said - That which the Tanna of the baraita teaches, "there is slaughter in its kind," he means [slaughter] by virtue of its mother, [meaning] that it is permitted through the slaughter of its mother:

Rashi on Chullin 74a:9:2.hebrew: מינא דאמיה לא פריך - לא חשיבא ליה פירכא, דהואיל ואין בבני ח' שחיטה, "אין במינו שחיטה" קרינא ביה:
Rashi on Chullin 74a:9:2.english: [The] kind of its mother cannot be used as a refutation - He does not consider it a refutation, for since there is no [valid] slaughter for eight-month-old [fetuses], we call it [a case of] "there is no slaughter in its kind."

Tosafot on Chullin 74a:10:1.hebrew: ולהאי תנא דקפריך טרפה דשחיטה מטהרתה מנא לן - קצת תימה, דכולא חדא ברייתא היא בת"כ, וידע רישא ולא ידע סיפא:
Tosafot on Chullin 74a:10:1.english: And according to that tanna who uses [it] as a refutation, from where do we [derive] that slaughter of a tereifa renders it pure - It is somewhat surprising, for it is all one baraita in Torat Kohanim, and [did] he know the first part and not know the latter part:

Tosafot on Chullin 74a:10:2.hebrew: נפקא ליה מדרב יהודה כו' - וא"ת: דתניא בס"פ רבי אליעזר דמילה (שבת דף קלו.): "לאכלה" — להביא בן ח' שאין שחיטתו מטהרתו, ורבי יוסי ור"א ברבי שמעון אומרים: שחיטתו מטהרתו. והשתא כולהו לא מתוקם כתנא דמתני', דאפילו ת"ק דהתם משמע דאי לאו "לאכלה", ה"א דשחיטה מטהרתו; ולתנא דמתני', בן ח', כיון דאין במינו שחיטה, ידעינן ליה מבהמה טמאה דאין שחיטה מטהרתה. אבל כתנא דברייתא דהכא מיתוקמא שפיר ת"ק דהתם, דכיון דיש במינו שחיטה אגב אמו, מיקרי שפיר יש במינו שחיטה ולא מצי למילף מבהמה טמאה, ולהכי צריך התם "לאכלה" למימר דאין שחיטה מטהרתו. ומיהו סוגיא דהתם לא אתיא כתנא קמא דברייתא דהכא, דרבא מפרש התם טעמא דרבי יוסי ורבי אליעזר, דסברי: בטרפה אע"ג דמתה היא דשחיטה מטהרתה, הכא נמי לא שנא; ורבנן — לא דמי לטרפה אפילו מן הבטן, דיש במינו שחיטה, הכא אין במינו שחיטה. ושמא תנא דמתניתין משום קרא ד"לאכלה" חשיב בן ח' אין במינו שחיטה. אי נמי, קרא ד"לאכלה" דדריש ת"ק התם הוי אסמכתא בעלמא; דהא לאביי דמוקי התם פלוגתייהו דפליגי — מר סבר חי הוא ומר סבר מת הוא — צריך לומר דאסמכתא היא, דכיון דחשיב ליה כמת, בלאו קרא אין שחיטתו מטהרתו:
Tosafot on Chullin 74a:10:2.english: He derives it from that of Rav Yehuda, etc. - And if you will say: For it was taught in a baraita at the end of the chapter [entitled] Rabbi Eliezer DeMilah (Shabbat 136a): "[Of which you may eat] for food" — [this comes] to include an animal born in the eighth [month of gestation], whose slaughter does not render it pure; and Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Elazar ben Rabbi Shimon say: Its slaughter renders it pure. Now, all of them [in that baraita] cannot be established according to the Tanna of our Mishnah, for even [according to] the first Tanna there, it is implied that were it not for [the word] "for food," I would have said that slaughter renders it pure; whereas according to the Tanna of our Mishnah, [regarding] an animal born in the eighth [month], since there is no slaughter in its kind, we derive it from an impure animal, whose slaughter does not render it pure. However, according to the Tanna of the baraita here, the first Tanna there is well established: for since there is slaughter in its kind by virtue of its mother, it is properly called "there is slaughter in its kind," and one cannot derive [it] from an impure animal; and therefore [the verse] "for food" is needed there to say that its slaughter does not render it pure. Nevertheless, the sugya there does not accord with the first Tanna of the baraita here, for Rava explains there the reason of Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Eliezer [ben Rabbi Shimon], who hold: Just as with a tereifa, even though it is [considered] dead, its slaughter renders it pure, here too it is no different; and the Rabbis [hold that] it is not comparable to a tereifa, even [one] from the womb, where there is slaughter in its kind — here there is no slaughter in its kind. Perhaps the Tanna of our Mishnah, because of the verse "for food," considers an animal born in the eighth [month] to be [one where] there is no slaughter in its kind. Alternatively, the verse "for food" that the first Tanna expounds there is a mere asmachta [scriptural support]; for according to Abaye, who establishes their dispute there as arguing [over whether] one Master holds it is alive and one Master holds it is dead, one must say that it is an asmachta, because since [the first Tanna] considers it as dead, even without a verse its slaughter does not render it pure:

Tosafot on Chullin 74a:1:1.hebrew: אין בהם אלא מצות פרוש בלבד - וקרא דברייתא אינו אלא אסמכתא בעלמא. וא"ת: וכיון דמדאורייתא שרי באכילה, אמאי נקט בברייתא דלעיל (חולין דף עג.) "לא, אם טיהרה שחיטת טרפה אותה ואת האבר המדולדל בה"? מה שייך שם להזכיר אבר מדולדל, דשרי אף באכילה? וי"ל דה"ק: אבר המדולדל בה — גזרו ביה רבנן איסור אכילה, ולא גזרו שלא תהא שחיטה מטהרתו, כמו עובר דבר שאינו גופה:
Tosafot on Chullin 74a:1:1.english: With regard to them, there is nothing other than a mitzva to separate - And the verse [cited in] the baraita is merely a support [asmakhta]. And if you ask: Since by Torah law it is permitted to be eaten, why did [the Tanna] state in the baraita above (Chullin 73a), "No, if the slaughter of a terefa rendered itself and the dangling limb on it pure"? What relevance is there there to mention a dangling limb, which is permitted even to be eaten? And one can answer that this is what it is saying: [Regarding] a dangling limb on it, the Rabbis decreed a prohibition on eating [it], but they did not decree that slaughter should not render it pure, as [is the case with] a fetus, which is something that is not part of its body:

Tosafot on Chullin 74a:6:1.hebrew: תרי במותם כתיבי - וא"ת: הא אכתי צריכי לכדדרשינן בהעור והרוטב (לקמן חולין דף קכח:): יכול בשר הפורש מן השרצים יהא טמא, תלמוד לומר "במותם" — מה מיתה שאינה עושה חליפין כו'? וי"ל: דכעין מותם וההיא דרשה מחד "במותם" נפקא. אי נמי, דרשה דהתם מ"נבלתם" נפקא: מה נבלה שאין עושה חליפין, ונקט "במותם" לפי שהיא דרשה פשוטה:
Tosafot on Chullin 74a:6:1.english: "When they are dead" is written twice - And if you say: Behold, they are still needed for that which we expound in [the chapter entitled] Ha'Or VeHaRotev (below, Chullin 128b): "One might think that flesh that separates from [living] creeping creatures is impure; the Torah states 'when they are dead' — just as death does not produce a replacement, etc."? And one can answer: [both] "similar to their death" and that exposition are derived from one "when they are dead." Alternatively, the exposition there is derived from "their carcass": just as a carcass does not produce a replacement, and [the Gemara there] cited "when they are dead" because it is a straightforward exposition:

Tosafot on Chullin 74a:7:1.hebrew: מחלוקת באבר דעובר חי - ובבן ח', דאילו בן ט' כשאר בהמה הוא לר"מ, וטעון שחיטה:
Tosafot on Chullin 74a:7:1.english: The dispute concerns the limb of a live fetus - And [specifically] regarding an eight-month [fetus]; for a nine-month [fetus] is like any other animal according to Rabbi Meir, and requires slaughter:
